candidate: cooperative yield between cached replanned WebAssembly atomic actions
site_deployment: Owner-private Site v64 unchanged; candidate served from a local Site source mirror

environment.browser: Zen 1.22.3b with a fresh isolated profile
environment.display: 1440x900 private Xvfb desktop with a visible browser window
environment.source_parity: Site mirror Arena.tsx, bot-reply.ts, and package.json byte-identical to candidate branch
environment.browser_capture: 12-20 fps X11 screen recording plus in-page requestAnimationFrame probe

observations: The visible-window recording captured BOT THINKING in painted frames during later bot replies.
The local match advanced from turn 1 to a terminal amber win at turn 11 without a UI error.
limitations: The frame probe covers one terminal reply on a fixed duel map, not a controlled distribution of procedural maps or both seats.
This is a local development server in Zen on Xvfb, not the owner-private in-app browser deployment or a device-representative browser latency benchmark.
There is no same-hardware synchronous baseline frame trace or predeclared responsiveness threshold; these observations do not establish a release-worthy improvement.
The observed game is a UI smoke test, not a complete-state trajectory parity or search-strength evaluation.
decision: Keep cooperative scheduling on the experimental branch and Site v64 unpublished until a controlled browser responsiveness and exact-action parity gate is complete.
